scope: Structured notices about advertised places, schools, institutions and services from the Deborah CSV and readable Occident advertising scans. This is a data extraction, not a public full-text archive.
limitations: Scan verification remains pending for OCR readings.
125 photographs required rotation before OCR. 26 photographs have undetermined orientation or low-confidence text and require manual review.
Mixed and mislabeled scans occur in the collection. File/folder dates alone are not accepted as publication dates.
Annual compilations with corrupt text layers and the June 1861 text layer need image-based checking; source filenames do not prove readable coverage.
A cited contact address may be a correspondence address, not the institution’s premises.
City points use existing cited locality coordinates; no historical street numbers were geocoded as modern addresses.
Proposals remain distinct from operating institutions. Jewish ownership and kosher status are not inferred from publication, surname or name-only matches.
excludedFalseMatches: Heilbronn complaint treated as hotel advertisement
Lewis Ellinger committee membership treated as M. Ellinger bookseller advertisement
Ritterband book-agency mention treated as boarding-house activity
Subscriber-payment acknowledgments treated as business activity

earlyReview.scope: All early OCR page records screened; upright pages read for missing named advertisements. Inverted/corrupted photographs are pending orientation-corrected OCR and were not treated as reliable negatives.
limits: A notice date printed without year is not promoted to a precise calendar date.
1851-11.pdf has potentially mixed issue pages:pp3–4containlater-lookingads.These are not used for new factual dates.
Existing named records in advertisements.json were excluded; repeated book-catalogue notices and agents lists were not expanded into imagined storefronts.
earlyReview.orientationCorrectionFollowUp: Corrected early photographs were re-screened. Remaining orientation-undetermined images are listed; some are covers or contain only collection watermarks. None was treated as proof of absence of advertisements.
